'''Ángel Fabián Di María''' ({{IPA|es|ˈaŋxel faˈβjan di maˈɾia}}; born 14 February 1988) is an Argentine professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|right winger]] or [[attacking midfielder]] for and [[captain (association football)|captain]]s [[Argentine Primera División]] club [[Rosario Central]]. Known for his dribbling and playmaking, he is regarded as one of the best wingers of his generation and one of Argentina's greatest ever players. He ranks as the all-time Argentine [[UEFA Champions League#Most assists|top assist provider]], and second overall, in the [[UEFA Champions League]] (41) and is [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]]'s [[List of Paris Saint-Germain FC records and statistics#Assists leaders|all-time top assist provider]] (112).<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=All-time Player {{!}} Most assists Stats {{!}} UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/rankings/players/assists/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> In addition, he is also one of a select number of players who have [[List of men's footballers with 1,000 or more official appearances|amassed over 1,000 career appearances]].

Di María began his career with [[Rosario Central]] but first came into prominence at [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] after signing for the club in 2007, aged 19. He helped Benfica win the [[Primeira Liga]], the club's first league title in five years, and two [[Taça da Liga]] titles. In 2010, Di María moved to Spanish club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in a transfer worth €25&nbsp;million, where he won the [[2011–12 La Liga]] title and the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|2013–14 Champions League]], amongst other honours. In 2014, Di María was selected in the [[FIFPRO#FIFA FIFPRO Men's World 11|FIFPRO Men's World 11]] and the [[UEFA Team of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Galloway |first=James |date=13 January 2015 |title=FIFPro World XI: Which 11 players made FIFA's team of the year for 2014? |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11096/9643492/fifpro-world-xi-which-11-players-made-fifas-team-of-the-year-for-2014}}</ref> After a falling out with the board at Madrid, he signed for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in 2014 in a then-British record deal worth £59.7&nbsp;million (€75.7&nbsp;million), and inherited the iconic number 7 shirt.

After only one season, Di María left England to join PSG in 2015. In his [[2015–16 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|debut season]], he scored the winning goal in the [[2016 Coupe de la Ligue final]] and set a [[Ligue 1]] record with 18 assists in a season, as he won his first of five French league titles as part of a [[domestic treble]]. In [[2017–18 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|2017–18]], he was the top scorer in the [[2017–18 Coupe de France|Coupe de France]] as PSG won the cup. In [[2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|2019–20]], Di María was integral in the club's [[2019–20 Ligue 1|Ligue 1]] title win and run to their first [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]], finishing as the top assist provider in both Ligue 1 and the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Di María is one of the club's [[List of Paris Saint-Germain F.C. records and statistics#All-time top scorers|top goalscorers]], with 92 goals. Since leaving PSG in 2022, he has joined Italian side [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], re-joined Benfica in 2023, and returned to Rosario in 2025, winning the [[AFA Liga Profesional de Fútbol|Primera División]] in his first season back.

Di María debuted for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] internationally in 2008. Playing for the [[Argentina national under-23 football team|country's Olympic team]] at the [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Olympic Games]], Di María scored the winning goal against [[Nigeria national under-23 football team|Nigeria]] in [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|the final]] to win Argentina their second successive [[Olympic medal|Olympic gold medal]] in football. He has 145 caps for his country, including appearing in ten major tournaments; he featured in four [[FIFA World Cup]]s for Argentina; helping his country reach [[2014 FIFA World Cup final|the final]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]] and win its third World Cup in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]], scoring the second goal in [[2022 FIFA World Cup final|the final]]. Furthermore, Di María was also part of the Argentina squads that reached four [[Copa América]] [[List of Copa América finals|finals]], in [[2015 Copa América|2015]], [[Copa América Centenario|2016]], [[2021 Copa América|2021]] and [[2024 Copa América|2024]], winning the latter two; he netted the only goal in the [[2021 Copa América final|2021 final]] to win Argentina their first trophy in 28 years. He retired from the national team after winning the [[2024 Copa América final]].

== Early life ==
Di María was born on 14 February 1988 in [[Rosario]], as one of three children of Miguel di María and Diana Hernandez, and grew up in Perdriel. As an infant, he was unusually active, and on the recommendation of a doctor was signed up for football at age three. He also helped his parents with their work at a local coal yard along with his two sisters, Vanesa and Evelyn. Due to the low income his family earned, purchasing football boots and keeping up with Di María's hobby was difficult for his parents. He considers himself to be a "family man" and has used a significant amount of his salary to "give back" to his family.<ref name=footballs>{{cite news |title=Angel Di Maria to Manchester United: Winger was once sold for 35 footballs – now it's £60m |first=Paul|last=Smith|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/angel-di-maria-to-manchester-united-the-winger-once-sold-for-35-footballs--now-its-60m-9690032.html |date=25 August 2014|newspaper=The Independent|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924045010/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/angel-di-maria-to-manchester-united-the-winger-once-sold-for-35-footballs--now-its-60m-9690032.html|archive-date=24 September 2014}}</ref> After being transferred to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], he asked his father not to work any more and purchased a house for his parents and sisters.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baier |first=Nicolas |date=2014-06-02 |title=Di Maria, the man who doesn't run alone |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37394822/the-man-run-alone |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Club career ==

=== Rosario Central ===
At age four, Di María joined [[Rosario Central]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chí |first=Minh |date=2014-08-27 |title=Hé lộ những sự thật thú vị về Di Maria |trans-title=Revealing interesting facts about Di Maria. |url=https://danviet.vn/he-lo-nhung-su-that-thu-vi-ve-di-maria-7777475058-d330626.html |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=danviet.vn}}</ref> As he had already committed to playing for his local club, Torito, 35 footballs were given in compensation.<ref name=footballs/>

Di María made his professional debut on 14 December 2005 in Rosario's final fixture of the [[Apertura and Clausura in Argentine football|Apertura]], a 2–2 draw away to [[Independiente de Avellaneda|Independiente]], by replacing [[Emiliano Vecchio]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cuatro goles para despedir el campeonato |trans-title=Four goals to see off the championship |url=http://www.espndeportes.com/futbol/cronica?id=187696 |publisher=ESPN |date=14 December 2005 |access-date=28 August 2014 |language=Spanish }}</ref> He scored for the first time on 24 November 2006 in the following season's Apertura in a 4–2 win at home over [[Quilmes Atlético Club|Quilmes]], a minute after replacing [[Leonardo Borzani]] at half-time.<ref>{{cite news |title=En casa es mucho mejor |trans-title=At home it's a lot better |url=http://www.espndeportes.com/futbol/cronica?id=204428 |publisher=ESPN |date=24 November 2006 |access-date=28 August 2014 |language=Spanish }}</ref> After playing at the [[2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in Canada, [[Boca Juniors]] made a bid of [[United States dollar|US$]]6.5&nbsp;million for him.<ref name=infobae>{{cite news |title=A Boca 'le soplaron' a Di María por la misma plata |trans-title=Boca "blew at" Di María for the same money |url=http://www.infobae.com/2007/07/27/328841-a-boca-le-soplaron-di-maria-la-misma-plata |publisher=Infobae |date=27 July 2007 |access-date=28 August 2014 |language=Spanish }}</ref> He was also approached by English club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], a move that fell through due to the United Kingdom's strict rules on issuing work permits to players from outside the [[European Union]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsene Wenger: Visa denied Arsenal's Angel Di Maria move |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30945201 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=23 January 2015 |access-date=25 January 2015 }}</ref>

=== Benfica ===
[[File:Ángel Di María (cropped Benfica).jpg|thumb|200x200px|Di María playing for [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in 2007]]
Di María was transferred to the Portuguese side Benfica in July 2007,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-07-05 |title=Angel di Maria: Argentina forward joins Benfica for second time |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66116139 |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> where he played as a winger. He was signed as a replacement for Benfica's departing captain, [[Simão Sabrosa|Simão]], who joined [[Atlético Madrid]] earlier that summer.<ref name=infobae/> Benfica paid Rosario Central €6 million for 80% of his sports rights and 50% of the sports rights of [[Andrés Díaz (Argentine footballer)|Andrés Díaz]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sport Lisboa e Benfica – Futebol, SAD announces an agreement in principle for the acquisition of Andrez Dias and Angel Di María. |url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR14437.pdf |work=SL Benfica |publisher=Published by CMVM |date=27 July 2007 |access-date=4 October 2010 |language=Portuguese |archive-date=7 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140107061050/http://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR14437.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Later, in August 2008, the Portuguese club paid an extra €2 million for the remaining 20%,<ref>{{cite news |title=Sport Lisboa e Benfica – Futebol SAD announces acquiring the remaining 20% of Di Maria's economic rights. |url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR19848.pdf |work=SL Benfica |publisher=Published by CMVM |date=13 August 2008 |access-date=4 October 2010 |language=Portuguese |archive-date=29 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729165721/https://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR19848.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> but re-sold 10% to [[GestiFute]].

Di María had his breakthrough in the 2009–10 season thanks to the trust placed in him by manager [[Jorge Jesus]]. On 22 October, in the [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League group stage#Group I|Europa League group stage]] match against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], he provided a hat-trick of assists for the first time in his career, in a 5–0 thrashing at the [[Estádio da Luz]], marking the biggest loss of an English side in a European competition.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brett |first=Oliver |date=2009-10-22 |title=Benfica 5-0 Everton |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/8318447.stm |access-date=2025-04-13 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=688188&sec=uefaeuropaleague&cc=5739 Europa League: Everton humbled, Fulham denied] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020121633/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=688188&sec=uefaeuropaleague&cc=5739 |date=20 October 2012 }}; ESPN Soccernet, 22 October 2009</ref> During that month, Di María signed a new deal with Benfica, adding three more years to his current deal, which was to last until 30 June 2015 with his release fee set at a minimum of €40&nbsp; million.<ref>{{cite news |date=2 October 2009 |title=Di Maria e a renovação: "É uma motivação mais." |trans-title=Di Maria and the renewal: "It's one more motivation." |url=http://www.slbenfica.pt/Informacao/Futebol/Noticias/noticiasfutebol_futdimariadec_021009_51868.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622224732/http://www.slbenfica.pt/Informacao/Futebol/Noticias/noticiasfutebol_futdimariadec_021009_51868.asp |archive-date=22 June 2017 |access-date=8 October 2009 |publisher=SL Benfica |language=Portuguese}}</ref> Afterwards, he was backed by [[Diego Maradona]] to become "Argentina's next superstar".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Football |first=Mirror |date=2009-10-27 |title=Chelsea transfer target Angel Di Maria will be a worldwide superstar, says Diego Maradona |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/chelsea-transfer-target-angel-di-3371948 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=The Mirror |language=en}}</ref> He would score a brace in Benfica's 2–1 home win over [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]], to ensure Benfica's qualification to the round of thirty-two, as group winners.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2000883--benfica-vs-aek-athens/ | title=History: Benfica-AEK Athens &#124; UEFA Europa League 2009/10 }}</ref>

On 27 February 2010, Di María scored his first hat-trick in a classic 4–0 win against [[Leixões S.C.|Leixões]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Second hat-trick for Di María |url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/en-us/agora/media-list/videos/2024/11/24/futebol-benfica-di-maria-dois-hat-tricks-com-a-camisola-do-glorioso?srsltid=AfmBOorxZm1W-SW2c9Uk1WVttlexkAA2tpG9VV2We4LD2GIUAC_faXVm |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=www.slbenfica.pt |language=en}}</ref> The next day, he made the headlines as "Magic Tri María" in all sports newspapers in Portugal.<ref>{{cite news |title=10 things you need to know about Liverpool target Angel De Maria |url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/opinion/blogs/mirror-football-blog/10-things-you-need-to-know-about-Liverpool-target-Angel-De-Maria-article161043.html |work=Mirror Football |date=17 September 2009 |access-date=1 July 2010 }}</ref> He finished as the league's top assister that season with 11 assists, including two in a 5–0 win against [[S.C. Olhanense|Olhanense]], as Benfica won the national championship, adding [[2009–10 Taça da Liga|the year]]'s [[Taça da Liga|domestic League Cup]], while being named Player of the Month in April.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/benfica/interior/benfica-conquista-o-32-titulo-da-historia-1565197.html|title=Benfica conquista o 32.º título da história|trans-title=Benfica conquer 32nd title in history|publisher=[[Diário de Notícias]]|first1=Gonçalo|last1=Lopes|first2=Tiago|last2=Silva Pires|language=pt|date=9 May 2010|access-date=21 May 2019}}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

=== Real Madrid ===

==== 2010–12: Debut season and La Liga win ====
[[File:Di María al Corner (5628107201).jpg|thumb|Di María against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in April 2011|243x243px]]On 28 June 2010, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] posted on their website that they had agreed with [[Benfica]] for the transfer of Di María. He signed a five-year contract for €25&nbsp; million, plus €11&nbsp; million in incentives, as announced one day later by the Portuguese Stock Exchange regulating entity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Official announcement |url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR29179.pdf |publisher=CMVM – Portuguese Securities Market Commission |date=28 June 2010 |access-date=16 July 2010 |language=Portuguese |archive-date=29 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729183106/https://web3.cmvm.pt/english/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR29179.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 7 July 2010, Di María arrived to [[Madrid]] directly from [[Buenos Aires]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Di Maria arrives in Madrid |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008824404/noticia/Noticia/Di_Maria_arrives_in_Madrid.htm |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=7 July 2010 |access-date=7 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100709231418/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008824404/noticia/Noticia/Di_Maria_arrives_in_Madrid.htm |archive-date=9 July 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and passed the medical test on 8 July.<ref>{{cite news |title=Di Maria passes physical |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008912924/noticia/Noticia/Di_Maria_passes_physical.htm |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |date=8 July 2010 |access-date=8 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100711112951/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330008912924/noticia/Noticia/Di_Maria_passes_physical.htm |archive-date=11 July 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut on 4 August 2010 in a friendly match against Mexican side [[Club América|América]], which Real Madrid won 3–2.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330010682535/noticia/Cronica/The_Whites_win_first_preseason_match.htm The Whites win first preseason match] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100919132737/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330010682535/noticia/Cronica/The_Whites_win_first_preseason_match.htm |date=19 September 2010 }} Real Madrid C.F., 5 August 2010.</ref> On 22 August, Di María scored his first goal in another friendly away against [[Hércules CF|Hércules]], which Real Madrid won 3–1.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2010/08/22/2082959/hercules-1-3-real-madrid-benzema-brace-seals-friendly Hercules v Real Madrid – Goal.com] ''Goal (website)'', 23 August 2010.</ref> In the last match of the pre-season, on 24 August, after an individual play described as a "magic moment", he opened the score of the 2–0 win against [[Peñarol]] for the [[Trofeo Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2010/08/24/2086070/real-madrid-2-0-penarol-hosts-win-sixth-successive-trofeo Real Madrid 2–0 Penarol: Hosts Win Sixth Successive Trofeo Santiago Bernabéu – Goal.com] ''Goal (website)'', 25 August 2010.</ref>

His [[2010–11 La Liga|league]] debut came on 29 August in a 0–0 draw against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302066&cc=3888 Report: Mallorca v Real Madrid – Spanish Primera División – ESPN Soccernet] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023112125/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302066&cc=3888 |date=23 October 2012 }} ESPN, 30 August 2010.</ref> On 18 September, Di María scored his first league goal for Real Madrid in their 2–1 away win over [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302003&cc=3888 Report: Real Sociedad 1 – 2 Real Madrid] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026105356/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302003&cc=3888 |date=26 October 2012 }} ESPN FC, 19 September 2010.</ref> Ten days later, he scored his first goal in the [[UEFA Champions League]] against [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] in a 1–0 victory.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/match/50431/aj-auxerre-vs-real-madrid/report Report: AJ Auxerre 0 – 1 Real Madrid] ''Goal (website)'', 28 September 2010.</ref> He scored a controversial first goal against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on 19 December. Days later, Di María assisted [[Karim Benzema]]'s two goals and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s goal in an astonishing 8–0 drubbing of [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 22 December. In the second leg of the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Champions League round of 16]] against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], he scored the third and final goal in a 3–0 win to send Real Madrid through to the quarter-finals for the first time in seven years.<ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Bryan |title=Jubilant Madrid breeze past Lyon |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01ef-0e778bbef7e8-9a236f8410f2-1000--jubilant-madrid-breeze-past-lyon/ |publisher=UEFA |date=16 March 2011 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref>

Di María scored Real Madrid's third goal during their first-leg [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|Champions League]] quarter-final victory over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on 5 April 2011.<ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Bryan |title=Majestic Madrid sweep Tottenham away |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f0-0e77b5d9628b-6bd653bf6381-1000--majestic-madrid-sweep-tottenham-away/ |publisher=UEFA |date=5 April 2011 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref> On 20 April, he was sent off in the 31st minute of extra time in the [[2011 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey final]] against rival [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. Real Madrid won the match 1–0, the lone goal of the match (in the 13th minute of extra time) being a header from Ronaldo, which came from his cross, thus obtaining his first honour with Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-04-20 |title=Ronaldo's late goal gives Real Madrid win over Barcelona in Copa del Rey |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/apr/21/real-madrid-barcelona-copa-del-rey |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

During the start of the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 season]], Di María endured a tough series of matches as he struggled to adapt to the pace of the league following the summer break. As a result, Di María's early performance for the season was mixed with moments of genuinely good play interspersed with moments of sheer madness by the Argentine. This point was well illustrated during Real Madrid's 1–0 defeat to Levante, a match which saw a clearly out-of-sorts Di María commit a horror foul on Levante's [[Juanfran (footballer, born 1976)|Juanfran]] during the match. Di María caused the two teams to clash and an on-field incident ensued. However, Di María's performances would improve, including opening up a significant gap at the top of the assists table. From October 2011, Di María was being picked by Madrid head coach [[José Mourinho]] ahead of [[Kaká]] and [[Mesut Özil]], a sign of his improving form.{{citation needed|date=February 2015}}

On 27 November 2011, Di María played 60 minutes in a league match against city rivals [[Atlético Madrid]], in which he scored a goal for Real Madrid. Mourinho's team won the match 4–1. On 3 December 2011, Di María scored Real's first goal from a sharp angle in a 3–0 defeat of [[Sporting de Gijón]] in La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |title=Real Madrid ease past Sporting Gijon 3–0 |url=http://ibnlive.in.com/news/real-madrid-ease-past-sporting-gijon-30/208452-5-21.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111206083001/http://ibnlive.in.com/news/real-madrid-ease-past-sporting-gijon-30/208452-5-21.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 December 2011 |publisher=IBN |date=3 December 2011 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref> He was a constant threat and presence in the starting XI as Real Madrid won their 32nd league title, playing in their 3–0 win over [[Athletic Bilbao]] that clinched the league title.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-05-02 |title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory over Athletic Bilbao |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17932028 |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== 2012–14: La Décima and Copa del Rey title ====
Di María scored his first goal of the season against Barcelona in the first leg of the [[2012 Supercopa de España]] at [[Camp Nou]] after a mistake by Barcelona goalkeeper [[Víctor Valdés]].<ref>{{cite news |title=The seven best Di Maria moments at Real Madrid |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2014/08/26/5061356/the-seven-best-di-maria-moments-at-real-madrid |work=Goal (website) |date=26 August 2014 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref> Although Di María did not have the best season, he did contribute in big moments, most notably by sending in the cross for Ronaldo's goal against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 13 February,<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=13 February 2013 |title=Real Madrid 1–1 Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21348206 |access-date=25 May 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation)}}</ref> he registered seventeen assists, and scored nine goals throughout the season in 52 appearances, notably against Atlético Madrid and [[Málaga CF|Málaga]]. On 9 August 2012, Di María signed a new contract with Real Madrid, keeping him at the club until 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Di Maria extends Real Madrid contract until 2018 |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2012/08/09/3297156/di-maria-extends-real-madrid-contract-until-2018 |work=Goal (website) |date=9 August 2012 |access-date=7 July 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2012-08-10 |title=Di Maria pens new Madrid deal |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2012/08/10/di-maria-pens-new-madrid-deal |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=Football España |language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Real Madrid vs Juventus, 24 October 2013 Champions League 29 (cropped).JPG|thumb|Di María preparing to take a free kick against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]] in October 2013]]
On 2 October 2013, Di María scored two goals against [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in Real Madrid's 4–0 Champions League victory over them.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/commentary/_/gameId/380761 |title=Real Madrid v FC Copenhagen |date=2 October 2013 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref> Later in the season, due to tactical decisions by the club's new manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]], Di María's playing position was permanently switched to that of an offensive–minded central midfielder, and he was frequently deployed in the starting line-up alongside [[Luka Modrić]] and [[Xabi Alonso]] in midfield in the team's 4–3–3 formation.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Paul Wilkes |date=2014-03-21 |title=How Angel di Maria went from England-bound castaway to key man at Real Madrid |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/how-angel-di-maria-went-england-bound-castaway-key-man-real-madrid#:WNGhruHhvHa0hA |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=fourfourtwo.com |language=en}}</ref> He contributed to the club's 2–1 victory over Barcelona in the [[2014 Copa del Rey Final]] with the opening goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Barcelona 1–2 Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27053737 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=16 April 2014 |access-date=17 April 2014 }}</ref> Di María was the top assist maker in La Liga for the season, contributing 17.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/stats/assists/_/league/esp.1/spanish-primera-division?cc=5739 |title=Spanish La Liga stats: Assists leaders – 2013–14 |work=ESPN FC |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures |access-date=17 May 2014 }}</ref>

In the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|2014 Champions League Final]] against Atlético Madrid on 24 May 2014, Di María dribbled past two players before producing a save from goalkeeper [[Thibaut Courtois]]. Di María's teammate [[Gareth Bale]], was there to head the rebound into the net in the 110th minute, giving Real Madrid a 2–1 lead over Atlético in an eventual 4–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Melero |first1=Delfín |last2=@delfinmelero |last3=Boxer |first3=Adapted by Jeffrey |last4=@jeffboxer |date=2016-05-24 |title=10 key moments from the 2014 Champions League final |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2016/05/24/57437ac2ca4741bf528b463f.html |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=MARCA English |language=en}}</ref> Di María was named [[man of the match]] by [[UEFA]] after the match, and was presented with the honour by former Manchester United head coach [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lovell |first1=Clare |title=Real's Di Maria says triumph makes sacrifice worthwhile |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-champions-di-maria-idINKBN0E503S20140525 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002084824/https://uk.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-champions-di-maria-idINKBN0E503S20140525 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 October 2020 |access-date=25 August 2020 |work=Reuters |date=25 May 2014}}</ref>

Di María was an unused substitute as Real Madrid won the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup]] against Sevilla on 12 August.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Rob |last1=Phillips |title=Super Cup: Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice in Real Madrid win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28741099 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=12 August 2014 |access-date=13 August 2014 }}</ref> A week later, in the first leg of the [[2014 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], he played the final 15 minutes of a 1–1 home draw against Atlético Madrid in place of Luka Modrić.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Staunton |first1=Peter |title=Scouting Report: Angel Di Maria |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2892/transfer-zone/2014/08/20/5047136/scouting-report-angel-di-maria |website=Goal (website) |access-date=25 August 2020 |date=20 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ashdown |first=John |date=2014-08-19 |title=Real Madrid 1-1 Atlético Madrid: Spanish Super Cup – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2014/aug/19/-sp-real-madrid-v-atletico-madrid-spanish-super-cup-live-report?page=with:block-53f3c3bfe4b0ab8524dca1db |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=the Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== Manchester United ===
On 26 August 2014, Di María signed a five-year deal with Manchester United for a transfer fee of £59.7&nbsp;million, [[List of most expensive association football transfers|one of the most expensive transfers of all time]] and the highest fee ever paid by a British club at the time.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |date=2014-08-26 |title=Ángel di María says Manchester United were the 'only club' after Real |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/26/angel-di-maria-completes-move-to-manchester-united |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Hirst |title=Angel di Maria to Manchester United: Premier League club sign Argentine winger in record £59.7m deal |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/angel-di-maria-to-manchester-united-latest-597m-winger-undergoing-medical-9690914.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/angel-di-maria-to-manchester-united-latest-597m-winger-undergoing-medical-9690914.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Independent |date=26 August 2014 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Ogden |title=Ángel di María signs for Manchester United in £59.7&nbsp;million deal |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/11056019/ngel-di-Maria-signs-for-Manchester-United-in-59.7-million-deal.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/11056019/ngel-di-Maria-signs-for-Manchester-United-in-59.7-million-deal.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Telegraph |date=26 August 2014 |access-date=26 August 2014 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> He inherited the number 7 shirt at United, which was previously worn by club legends such as [[George Best]], [[Bryan Robson]], [[Eric Cantona]], [[David Beckham]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonnell |first=David |date=2007-09-28 |title=Cristiano Ronaldo exclusive |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/cristiano-ronaldo-exclusive-716711 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=The Mirror |language=en}}</ref> However, he said in an open letter to Real Madrid fans that he had never wanted to leave Real Madrid, but that its board had been unsupportive and unfair: "Someone may not like me".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |date=2014-08-27 |title=Ángel di María admits: It was never my desire to leave Real Madrid |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/27/angel-di-maria-manchester-united-real-madrid-letter |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Di María made his debut on 30 August in a 0–0 draw with [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], in which he was substituted for [[Anderson (footballer, born 1988)|Anderson]] after 70 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Ogden |title=Angel Di Maria makes his Premier League debut |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/11065565/Angel-Di-Maria-makes-his-Premier-League-debut-how-did-he-fare-in-Manchester-Uniteds-draw-at-Burnley.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/11065565/Angel-Di-Maria-makes-his-Premier-League-debut-how-did-he-fare-in-Manchester-Uniteds-draw-at-Burnley.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Telegraph |date=30 August 2014 |access-date=30 August 2014 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> He scored his first goal for United on 14 September, netting directly from a free-kick in a 4–0 win over [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref name="MUTD- QPR">{{cite news |title=Manchester United click again as they crush Queens Park Rangers |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/313422/report |work=Sky Sports |date=14 September 2014 |access-date=14 September 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd 4–0 QPR |url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2014-2015/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-qpr |publisher=Premier League |date=14 September 2014 |access-date=14 September 2014 |archive-date=15 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140915164922/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2014-2015/epl.match-report.html/man-utd-vs-qpr |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also provided an assist for [[Juan Mata]]'s goal in the same match, winning the vote for Man of the Match.<ref name="MUTD- QPR" /> His performance was highlighted by [[Sky Sports]]' ''Player Cam'' feature, which was brought back especially for the match.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Bate |title=Angel di Maria shows why he can be the difference maker for Manchester United in emphatic 4–0 win over QPR |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/15115/9470677/angel-di-maria-shows-why-he-can-be-the-difference-maker-for-manchester-united-in-emphatic-4-0-win-over-qpr |work=Sky Sports |date=14 September 2014 |access-date=17 September 2014 }}</ref> In the next match, against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] on 21 September, he again scored a goal and provided another assist, although United lost the match 5–3.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Aimee |last1=Lewis |title=Leicester 5–3 Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29196081 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=21 September 2014 |access-date=14 October 2014 }}</ref>

On 2 October, Di María won Manchester United's Player of the Month award for September after recording two goals and two assists in his first four matches for the club.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Gemma |last1=Thompson |first2=James |last2=Tuck |title=Di Maria wins Player of the Month prize |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2014/Oct/angel-di-maria-is-named-united-player-of-the-month-for-september.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=2 October 2014|access-date=14 October 2014 }}</ref> One week later, he won his second individual trophy at United after his goal against Leicester, in which he chipped goalkeeper [[Kasper Schmeichel]], was voted as the club's Goal of the Month for September.<ref>{{cite news |first=James |last=Tuck |title=Di Maria wins Goal of the Month award |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2014/Oct/angel-di-maria-vs-leicester-wins-manchester-united-goal-of-the-month-for-september-2014.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=9 October 2014 |access-date=21 February 2015 }}</ref> Di María continued his run of fine form on 5 October by scoring a goal and providing an assist for [[Radamel Falcao]] to help United defeat [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Mike |last1=Henson |title=Man Utd 2–1 Everton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29398862 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=5 October 2014 |access-date=14 October 2014 }}</ref> Di María was substituted with a hamstring injury 13 minutes into United's 3–0 defeat of [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] on 29 November and made only one substitute appearance in the team's next seven matches.

On 4 January 2015, Di María returned from injury to score a late goal in a 2–0 win against [[Yeovil Town F.C.|Yeovil Town]] in the third round of the [[2014–15 FA Cup|FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Yeovil 0–2 Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/30670662 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=4 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015 }}</ref> A week later, he was used as a forward by manager [[Louis van Gaal]] in a 1–0 home defeat to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd 0–1 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30670763 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=11 January 2015 |access-date=23 January 2015 }}</ref> This new role came in the midst of a bad run of form for Di María, who was said to have struggled since October.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stanger |first=Matthew |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11660/9740063/why-is-angel-di-maria-struggling-to-discover-his-best-form-for-manchester-united-this-season |title=Why is Angel di Maria struggling to discover his best form for Manchester United this season? |date=2 March 2015 |access-date=2 March 2015 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> Di María was sent off on 9 March as United lost 2–1 at home against Arsenal in the [[2014–15 FA Cup|FA Cup sixth round]], being booked for diving and for grabbing the shirt of referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]], but earlier set up the equaliser by [[Wayne Rooney]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=9 March 2015 |title=Manchester United 1–2 Arsenal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31689011 |access-date=9 March 2015 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonnell |first=David |date=2015-03-09 |title=Louis van Gaal: Angel Di Maria can have 'no excuses' over red card |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/louis-van-gaal-angel-di-5302330 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=Daily Mirror |language=en}}</ref> At the season's end, Di María was judged by ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' to be the worst signing of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-05-21 |title=20 worst Premier League signings of the 2014/15 season |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/11616110/20-worst-Premier-League-signings-of-the-201415-season.html?frame=3310751 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=The Telegraph |language=en}}</ref>

=== Paris Saint-Germain ===

==== 2015–19: Transfer and domestic success ====
[[File:Chelsea FC vs Paris Saint-Germain, 9 March 2016 (25367124690).jpg|left|thumb|250x250px|Di María with [[Paris Saint-Germain]] during the Champions League match against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in March 2016]]
On 25 July 2015, Di María failed to board a flight to the United States to join Manchester United's pre-season tour as scheduled; manager Louis van Gaal said he "did not know why".<ref>{{cite web|title=Angel Di Maria not on flight to join up with Man United on tour|url=http://www.espnfc.com/manchester-united/story/2536641/angel-di-maria-misses-flight-to-join-up-with-man-united|publisher=ESPN FC|access-date=1 August 2015|date=25 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |date=2015-07-25 |title=Ángel Di María fails to make flight to join Manchester United on tour |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/jul/26/angel-di-maria-manchester-united-paris-saint-germain |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Observer |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref> On 2 August, it was reported Di María would undergo a medical ahead of a move to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]];<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33750886 |title=Angel Di Maria: Man Utd winger set for Paris St-Germain medical |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=2 August 2015 |first=Simon |last=Stone |access-date=2 August 2015}}</ref> and four days later, Manchester United confirmed he had been sold to the [[2014–15 Ligue 1|French champions]] for an undisclosed fee, believed to be around £44&nbsp;million, signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Manchester United completes sale of Angel Di Maria to Paris-Saint Germain |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2015/Aug/manchester-united-completes-sale-of-angel-di-maria-to-paris-saint-germain.aspx |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=6 August 2015 |access-date=6 August 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Angel Di Maria signs for Paris Saint-Germain until 2019 |url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/71811/Angel-Di-Maria-signs-for-Paris-Saint-Germain-until-2019 |website=psg.fr |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain FC |date=6 August 2015 |access-date=6 August 2015 |archive-date=25 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170625043447/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/71811/Angel-Di-Maria-signs-for-Paris-Saint-Germain-until-2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Di Maria completes £44m PSG move |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33681538 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=6 August 2015 |access-date=6 August 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.psg.fr/effectif/angel-di-maria?season=2017|title=Angel Di Maria|website=psg.fr|publisher=Paris Saint-Germain|access-date=19 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819190723/https://en.psg.fr/effectif/angel-di-maria?season=2017|archive-date=19 August 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Di María made his [[Ligue 1]] debut on 30 August away to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] as a 66th-minute substitute for [[Lucas Moura|Lucas]], and assisted [[Ezequiel Lavezzi]] for the final goal of a 3–0 win at the [[Stade Louis II]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-08-30 |title=Monaco 0-3 Paris St-Germain |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34102735 |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 15 September, Di María scored his first goal for PSG on his Champions League debut for the club, a 2–0 win over [[Malmö FF]] at the [[Parc des Princes]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.us/uefa-champions-league/match/434269/paris-saint-germain-malmo-ff/report|title=Angel Di Maria scores first PSG goal in Champions League win against Malmo|date=15 September 2015|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Seven days later, he registered his first goal in Ligue 1 as PSG defeated [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]] 3–0.<ref>{{Cite news |agency=Press Association |date=2015-09-22 |title=Ángel Di María on target as Paris Saint-Germain beat Guingamp |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/sep/22/paris-saint-germain-guingamp-match-report |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On 23 April 2016, Di María scored the winning goal for PSG in the [[2016 Coupe de la Ligue Final]] against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] at the [[Stade de France]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36121198|title=Paris St-Germain beat Lille 2–1 in the Coupe de la Ligue final|date=23 April 2016|publisher=BBC}}</ref> Di María ended [[2015–16 Ligue 1|2015–16]] setting a new [[List of Ligue 1 records and statistics|Ligue 1 record]] for [[Assist (football)|assists]] in a season with 18.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1722/ligue-1/2016/05/14/23532522/di-maria-sets-new-ligue-1-record-with-18-assists|title=Di Maria sets new Ligue 1 record with 18 assists|date=14 May 2016|work=Goal (website)}}</ref>
[[File:Toulouse IMG 0015 (40263378631) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Di María (centre) with teammates [[Dani Alves]] (left) and [[Marquinhos]] (right) prior to a [[Ligue 1]] match in February 2018 ]]
In the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League group stage|2016–17 Champions League group stage]] home match against [[FC Basel|Basel]] on 19 October 2016, Di María scored the opening goal in the 40th minute in a 3–0 victory for PSG to register his first goal of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/psg-vs-basel/2348318/report|title=Paris Saint-Germain vs Basel, 2016–2017 UEFA Champions League Group stage|work=Goal (website)|date=19 October 2016}}</ref> On 19 November, he opened the scoring with his first [[2016–17 Ligue 1|Ligue 1]] goal of the season in a 2–0 home win against [[FC Nantes|Nantes]].

On 14 February 2017, Di María scored a brace as PSG defeated Barcelona 4–0 in the first leg of [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|2016–17 UEFA Champions League round of 16]] at the Parc des Princes.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0233-0e95a6827229-c2408b81eeeb-1000--ronaldo-decides-madrid-derby-dortmund-beat-bayern/|title=Ronaldo decides Madrid derby, Dortmund beat Bayern|publisher=UEFA|date=19 November 2016}}</ref> On 1 April, he scored in PSG's 4–1 win over Monaco in the [[2017 Coupe de la Ligue final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ligue1.com/coupeLigue/feuille_match/82777–|title=AS Monaco 4–1 Paris Saint-Germain|date=1 April 2017|work=Ligue 1}}</ref> On 8 May 2018, he played as PSG won 2–0 against [[Les Herbiers VF|Les Herbiers]] to clinch the [[2017–18 Coupe de France]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |title=French Cup final – PSG beat Les Herbiers |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/43949707 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2018 |access-date=12 April 2019 }}</ref>

On the first leg of his side's [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|Champions league round of 16]] tie against his former club Manchester United in the 2018–19 season, Di María sustained a serious injury following a tackle from [[Ashley Young]]; however, he refused to be substituted, and in the final moments of the game, he assisted [[Kylian Mbappé]]'s goal for a 2–0 win at [[Old Trafford]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-02-13 |title=Champions League Extra Time: Manchester United's horror night as Gianluigi Buffon enters top 10 |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/uefa-champions-league/champions-league-extra-time-manchester-uniteds-horror-night-as-gianluigi-buffon-enters-top-10/news-story/d36cbe06f14dc5f324ffb97e54caec54 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=Fox Sports |language=en}}</ref> Eventually, PSG lost 3–1 in the second leg and were eliminated in the round of 16 for the third consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite news|title=You have to give Solskjaer the job after that|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47477664|access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref>

==== 2019–2022: European final, assist record and departure ====
[[File:LOSC chinese new year (cropped trio).jpg|thumb|Di María (left) during a Ligue 1 match against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in January 2020]]
In the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|2019–20 Champions League]] group stage, Di María scored a brace in a 3–0 win over his former club Real Madrid on 18 September 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2027025--paris-vs-real-madrid/ |title=Paris 3–0 Real Madrid |publisher=UEFA |date=18 September 2019 }}</ref> On 18 August 2020, Di María scored a goal and recorded two assists in PSG's 3–0 Champions League semi-final victory over [[RB Leipzig]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendola |first=Nicholas |date=2020-08-18 |title=Di Maria shines as PSG crushes RB Leipzig |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/di-maria-shines-as-psg-crushes-rb-leipzig |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> the club went on to play against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|final]], but lost the match 1–0.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |title=Bayern beat PSG to win Champions League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53867676 |access-date=16 September 2020 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 23 September 2020, Di María was handed a four-match suspension for a spitting incident with [[Álvaro González (footballer, born 1990)|Álvaro González]] during ''[[Le Classique]]'' 10 days earlier.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PSG star Di Maria handed four-match ban for spitting incident during Ligue 1 loss to Marseille {{!}} Goal.com|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/psg-di-maria-four-match-ban-for-spitting/19s4y53z7bacp10gif93g0kci6|access-date=24 September 2020|website=Goal (website)}}</ref> He would miss the league matches against [[Angers SCO|Angers]], [[Nîmes Olympique|Nîmes]], [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]] and [[FC Nantes|Nantes]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fixtures and Results|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/fixtures-and-results|access-date=24 September 2020|website=psg.fr}}</ref> In a UEFA Champions League match against RB Leipzig on 4 November, Di María scored the opening goal in an eventual 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-11-04 |title=RB Leipzig 2-1 Paris St-Germain: Idrissa Gueye and Presnel Kimpembe sent off for French champions |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54812745 |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his return to league action in a match against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] three days later, and scored a goal to help PSG win the match 3–0.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Paris Saint-Germain vs. Stade Rennes – Football Match Report – November 7, 2020 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=573181|access-date=15 November 2020|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

In a home match against [[İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.|İstanbul Başakşehir]] on 9 December 2020, Di María recorded two assists; he subsequently became the player with the third most assists in Champions League history with a tally of 32, only being behind [[Lionel Messi]] and Ronaldo.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zavala|first=Steve|date=10 December 2020|title=Only Ronaldo and Messi Have Recorded More Champions League Assists Than Di Maria|url=https://psgtalk.com/2020/12/only-ronaldo-and-messi-have-recorded-more-champions-league-assists-than-di-maria/|access-date=|website=PSG Talk}}</ref> On 12 March 2021, Di María extended his contract with Paris Saint-Germain for one more season with an option for a second.<ref>{{Cite web|date=12 March 2021|title=Angel Di Maria prolonge jusqu'en 2022|url=https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/angel-di-maria-prolonge-son-contrat-avec-le-paris-saint-germain-jusquen-2022|access-date=12 March 2021|website=Paris Saint-Germain|language=fr}}</ref> On 4 May, Di María was sent off against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the semi-finals of the Champions League for stamping on [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandinho]] in an off the ball incident.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zavala|first=Steve|date=10 December 2020|title=Angel Di Maria given straight red card after losing head|url=https://www.givemesport.com/1686287-man-city-vs-psg-angel-di-maria-given-straight-red-card-after-losing-head|access-date=4 May 2021|website=GiveMeSport}}</ref> He was handed a three-match ban in European competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|date=8 September 2021|title=Man City handed boost as Angel Di Maria banned for three Champions League clashes|url=https://www.101greatgoals.com/news/manchester-city-handed-boost-as-angel-di-maria-banned-for-three-champions-league-clashes/|access-date=20 September 2021|website=101 Great Goals|archive-date=19 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019025738/https://www.101greatgoals.com/news/manchester-city-handed-boost-as-angel-di-maria-banned-for-three-champions-league-clashes/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the [[2021 Coupe de France Final]], when PSG defeated Monaco by a score of 2–0, Di María broke the all-time assist record for PSG by delivering a pass for a Kylian Mbappé goal. It was his 104th assist as a PSG player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2021 |title=PSG. Di Maria devient le meilleur passeur de l'histoire du club |trans-title=PSG. Di María becomes the best passer in the history of the club |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/paris-sg/psg-di-maria-devient-le-meilleur-passeur-de-l-histoire-du-club-f4d713e8-b94f-11eb-a0fd-a22b595c4b48 |access-date=20 May 2022 |website=Ouest-France |language=fr}}</ref> 

In the [[2021–22 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2021–22 season]] with Paris Saint-Germain, Di María won the Ligue 1 title, his fifth league title with the club. On 20 May 2022, his departure from Paris at the end of his contract was confirmed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 May 2022 |title=Paris Saint-Germain thanks Angel Di Maria |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/paris-saint-germain-thanks-angel-di-maria-2021-2022 |access-date=20 May 2022 |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain F.C. |archive-date=20 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220520212626/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/paris-saint-germain-thanks-angel-di-maria-2021-2022 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In his last match for the club against [[FC Metz|Metz]] on 21 May, Di María scored a goal and recorded an assist, helping his team to a 5–0 win. He received a tribute and ovation from the Parc des Princes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 May 2022 |title=Des larmes, de la joie et du show : dernière sortie réussie pour Paris |trans-title=Tears, happiness and a show: last successful outing for Paris |url=https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/des-larmes-de-la-joie-et-du-show-derniere-sortie-reussie-pour-paris-compte-rendu-resume-paris-saint-germain-metz-psg-ligue-1 |access-date=21 May 2022 |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain F.C. |language=fr}}</ref> Di María ended his spell at PSG with 92 goals and 112 assists in 295 matches.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.zyri.net/2022/05/21/the-disconsolate-cry-of-jorgelina-cardoso-at-the-farewell-of-angel-di-maria-from-psg/ |title=The disconsolate cry of Jorgelina Cardoso at the farewell of Ángel Di María from PSG |date=21 May 2022 |access-date=21 May 2022 |website=Zyri}}</ref>

=== Juventus ===
On 8 July 2022, Di María joined [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] as a [[free agent]] after signing an annual contract.<ref>{{cite web|date=8 July 2022|title=Official {{!}} Angel Di Maria Signs for Juventus|url=https://www.juventus.com/en/news/articles/official-angel-di-maria-signs-for-juventus|access-date=8 July 2022|publisher=Juventus FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-07-08 |title=Angel di Maria joins Juventus on free transfer after leaving Paris St-Germain |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62102320 |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made his club debut on 15 August, in Juventus's opening match of the Serie A season; he scored the opening goal and later assisted [[Dušan Vlahović]]'s second goal in an eventual 3–0 home win but was substituted in the second half after sustaining an injury.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bettoni |first1=Lorenzo |date=15 August 2022 |title=Juventus: Di Maria subbed off with suspected adductor injury |url=https://football-italia.net/juventus-di-maria-subbed-off-with-suspected-adductor-injury/ |access-date=16 August 2022 |website=Football Italia}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Horncastle |first=James |date=16 August 2022 |title=Angel Di Maria's Juventus debut: Goal, assist, rabona, injury |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3509852/2022/08/16/angel-di-maria-juventus-debut/ |access-date=20 August 2022 |website=The Athletic}}</ref> On 15 September, he made his [[List of footballers with 100 or more UEFA Champions League appearances|100th Champions League appearance]], and his debut with Juventus in that competition, in a 2–1 home defeat against his former club Benfica.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0257-0e9a10f58015-92c648e6303d-1000--who-has-played-100-champions-league-games/ |title=Who has played 100 Champions League games? |publisher=UEFA |date=15 September 2022 }}</ref> On 5 October, Di María provided a hat-trick of assists in a 3–1 home win against [[Maccabi Haifa FC|Maccabi Haifa]] in the Champions League, making the [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#Most assists|third highest assist provider]] in the competition's history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Champions-League/05-10-2022/juve-maccabihaifa-diretta-champions-risultato-live-450491383444.shtml|title=FINALE Juve-Maccabi Haifa 3-1: doppietta di Rabiot e tre assist di Di Maria, prima vittoria in Champions|website=La Gazzetta dello Sport|date=5 October 2022|access-date=8 January 2023}}</ref> Despite his contributions, Juventus finished third in the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] which put them in the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|knockout round play-offs]], and as a result, they failed to make the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|Champions League knockout stages]] for the first time since 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2021-2022/benfica-v-juventus-champions-league-live_sto9200818/story.shtml|title=BENFICA 4-3 JUVENTUS: BENFICA THROUGH TO LAST 16 AFTER CLINGING ON FOR VICTORY BUT JUVE OUT OF CHAMPIONS LEAGUE|website=[[EuroSport]]|date=26 October 2022|access-date=8 January 2023}}</ref>

On 23 February 2023, he scored a hat-trick in a 3–0 away win over Nantes in the [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Emons |first=Michael |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64752260 |title=Nantes 0–3 Juventus |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 February 2023}}</ref> On 9 March, he scored his fourth goal in the competition, after netting the only goal of a home win over [[SC Freiburg|Freiburg]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-09 |title=Il primo round va alla Juve: col Friburgo ci pensa il solito Di Maria |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Juventus/09-03-2023/europa-league-juve-friburgo-1-0-gol-di-maria-460588343751.shtml |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it-IT}}</ref> He impressed during the season, despite suffering from multiple hamstring injuries, which limited his game time. On 6 June, Di María confirmed his departure from Juventus, following the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Susy Campanale|url=https://football-italia.net/di-maria-announces-he-is-leaving-juventus/|title=Di Maria announces he is leaving Juventus|date=6 June 2023}}</ref>
=== Return to Benfica ===
[[File:Di Maria diz que escolheu voltar ao Benfica “com o coração”.webm|thumb|Di María with [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in 2023]]Amidst growing interest from Saudi clubs, Di María ended all speculations on 6 July 2023, when he signed a one-year contract with Benfica and was presented in front of 2,500 Benfica supporters in the entrance of [[Estádio da Luz]].<ref>{{cite news|date=6 July 2023|title=Bem-vindo, Di María!|trans-title=Welcome, Di María!|url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/pt-pt/agora/noticias/2023/07/06/futebol-benfica-direto-apresentacao-di-maria|language=pt|work=S.L. Benfica|access-date=5 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Abola.pt |date=2023-07-06 |title=Benfica O regresso do herói no balcão real do Sport Argentina e Benfica {{!}} Abola.pt |trans-title=Benfica – The return of the hero at the royal counter of Sport Argentina and Benfica {{!}} Abola.pt |url=https://www.abola.pt/futebol/noticias/o-regresso-do-heroi-no-balcao-real-do-sport-argentina-e-benfica-2023080919585547164 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=Abola.pt |language=pt}}</ref>

On 9 August, Di María made his second debut at Benfica, scoring the opening goal of a 2–0 victory over [[FC Porto|Porto]] in the [[2023 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira|Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira]], winning his first trophy back with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/id/berita/angel-di-maria-and-petar-musa-on-target-as-benfica-beat-porto-2-0-in-the-super-cup-38006246 |title=Ángel Di María and Petar Musa on target as Benfica beat Porto 2-0 in the Super Cup |publisher=OneFootball |date=9 August 2023 }}</ref> With two assists and a goal in a 4–0 win over [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]] on 2 September, he reached five goal contributions in his first four league games.<ref>{{cite web |date=2 September 2023 |title=Kokçu estreia-se a marcar pelo SL Benfica com fantástico golo |trans-title=Kokçu scores his first goal for SL Benfica with a fantastic strike. |url=https://bolanarede.pt/especial-bola-na-rede/ultima-hora/kokcu-estreia-se-a-marcar-pelo-sl-benfica-com-fantastico-golo/ |access-date=3 September 2023 |publisher=Bola na Rede |language=pt}}</ref> On 29 September, he scored the only goal of a home win over Porto, in the Primeira Liga, allowing his side to stay on top of the league table.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 September 2023 |title=Di María decide mais uma vez e Benfica vence Porto no Campeonato Português |trans-title=Di María decides once again and Benfica defeats Porto in the Portuguese Championship. |url=https://trivela.com.br/portugal/di-maria-benfica-porto-classico/}}</ref> In the last [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group D|Champions League group stage match]] on 12 December, Di María scored his first goal in the competition with Benfica, directly from a corner kick, in a 3–1 away win over [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]], which proved essential for the ''Eagles'' to qualify to the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League knock-out round play-offs]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 December 2023 |title=A redenção de Arthur Cabral: entrou aos 90'+1 e decidiu um minuto depois com este golo de calcanhar |trans-title=Arthur Cabral's redemption: came on at 90'+1 and was decisive one minute later with this back-heel goal |url=https://www.record.pt/internacional/competicoes-de-clubes/liga-dos-campeoes/detalhe/arthur-cabral-apura-benfica-entrou-aos-901-e-decidiu-aos-903-com-este-golo-de-calcanhar |access-date=12 December 2023 |publisher=Record |language=pt-PT}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/soccer/futbol/video/benficas-angel-di-maria-scores-olimpico-corner-kick-goal |title=Watch Angel Di Maria Score Direct From Corner Kick For Benfica Against RB Salzburg |website=si.com |date=12 December 2023 }}</ref> There, he scored two penalties in a 2–1 aggregate victory over [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mundoalbiceleste.com/2024/02/16/angel-di-maria-scores-twice-for-benfica-in-2-1-win-vs-toulouse/ |title=Ángel Di María scores twice for Benfica in 2-1 win vs. Toulouse |website=mundoalbiceleste.com |date=16 February 2024 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref> In the first leg of the quarter-finals against Olympique de Marseille on 11 April, he scored from open play to help his side to a 2–1 victory,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mundoalbiceleste.com/2024/04/11/angel-di-maria-scores-for-benfica-in-2-1-win-vs-marseille/ |title=Ángel Di María scores for Benfica in 2-1 win vs. Marseille |website=mundoalbiceleste.com |date=11 April 2024 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref> but in the second leg, he missed the first kick of the penalty shootout as Benfica was knocked-out.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-au/football/uefa-europa-league/articles-video/marseille-edges-benfica-on-penalties-2024-04-19 |title=Marseille edges Benfica on penalties |website=www.beinsports.com |date=19 April 2024 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref>

On 23 November 2024, the 36-year-old Di María scored a 16-minute hat-trick in the opening 18 minutes of the Portuguese Cup fourth round match against [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]], helping his team to a 7–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mundoalbiceleste.com/2024/11/23/angel-di-maria-scores-a-hat-trick-in-18-minutes-for-benfica/ |title=Ángel Di María scores a hat trick in 18 minutes for Benfica |website=mundoalbiceleste.com |date=23 November 2024 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref> Two months later, on 11 January, he started in the [[2025 Taça da Liga final]] against city rivals Sporting, converting his penalty in an eventual shoot-out victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://rr.pt/bola-branca/extralarge/sporting/2025/01/11/benfica-conquista-a-taca-da-liga-ao-sporting-nos-penaltis/409178/ |title=Benfica conquista a Taça da Liga ao Sporting nos penáltis |trans-title=Benfica wins the League Cup against Sporting on penalties |language=pt |website=rr.pt |date=11 January 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref> Di María scored four penalties in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]], the first three against Boca Juniors and [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup group stage|group stage]], while the fourth was a last-minute equaliser against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the round of 16, which ended in a 4–1 loss in extra-time. This marked the end of his European career, after 768 official matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-daily-stats-club-world-cup-4459 |title=Club World Cup statistics (Round of 16, 28 June) |publisher=[[IFFHS]] |date=29 June 2025 |access-date=2 July 2025 }}</ref>

=== Return to Rosario Central ===
On 29 May 2025, it was announced by boyhood club [[Rosario Central]] that Di María would be returning on a free transfer after Benfica's participation in the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Mantej |last=Mann |title=Di Maria to return to boyhood club despite previous threats |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cg5vmp6n3zpo |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2025 |access-date=29 May 2025}}</ref> On 12 July, he made his first appearance since returning to the club, scoring a penalty in a 1–1 draw against [[Godoy Cruz Antonio Tomba|Godoy Cruz]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/liga-profesional-argentina/articles/di-mar%C3%ADa-scores-and-gets-injured-in-his-emotional-debut-with-rosario-central-2025-07-12 |title=Di María Scores and Gets Injured in His Emotional Debut With Rosario Central |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=13 July 2025 }}</ref> On 29 June 2026, Di María extended his contract with Rosario Central until June 2027.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ángel Di María sigue en Central: renovó por una temporada más |url=https://www.lacapital.com.ar/ovacion/angel-di-maria-sigue-central-renovo-una-temporada-mas-n10267060.html |work=La Capital |date=29 June 2026 |access-date=31 August 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

== International career ==

=== 2007–2008: Success at youth level ===
In 2007, Di María was picked to play for the [[Argentina national under-20 football team|Argentina under-20 team]]. He was capped for the [[2007 South American U-20 Championship]] in Paraguay. In 2007, he was called up for the [[2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in Canada. They went on to win the tournament with Di María scoring three goals in the process.<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina's joy of six |url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/u20worldcup/canada2007/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903134332/http://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/u20worldcup/canada2007/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 September 2014 |publisher=FIFA.com (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) |access-date=27 August 2014 }}</ref>

On 28 January 2008, Di María and some of his under-20s teammates were called up for the [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina Olympic football team]] for the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]]. He scored the extra-time game-winning goal on a pass from [[Lionel Messi]] in the 105th minute of his team's 2–1 quarter-final win over the Netherlands.<ref>{{cite web |title=Argentina 2:1 Netherlands |url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/mensolympic/beijing2008/matches/round=250022/match=300051809/report.html |publisher=FIFA.com (Fédération Internationale de Football Association) |date=16 August 2014 |access-date=27 August 2014 }}</ref> On 23 August, Di María scored the game-winner – a chip over the goalkeeper from the edge of the area – in the 57th minute of Argentina's 1–0 victory against [[Nigeria national under-23 football team|Nigeria]] to capture their second-straight Olympic gold medal in the final game of the Olympic tournament.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Richard |date=2008-08-23 |title=Olympics: Di Maria winner earns gold for Argentina |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/23/olympics2008.argentina |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== 2008–2010: Senior debut and early national team career ===
[[File:Angel di Maria (L), Raul Meireles (R), Portugal - Argentina, 9th February 2011.jpg|thumb|Di María (left) and [[Raul Meireles]] (right) battle for the ball during a friendly match between [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] and [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] in February 2011.]]

On 6 September 2008, Di María made his debut for the [[Argentina national football team|Argentina senior team]] in a match against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]].<ref name=fifa>{{cite web |title=Angel Di Maria |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player=266800/profile-detail.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140615102205/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player=266800/profile-detail.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 June 2014 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=26 August 2014 }}</ref>

On 19 May 2010, Di María was selected by Argentinian manager [[Diego Maradona]] in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup squads#Argentina|23-man squad]] for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] in South Africa. On 24 May, Di María scored his debut international goal in a 5–0 [[Friendly (association football)|friendly]] win over [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 May 2010 |title=Argentina 5 Canada 0: match report |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/argentina/7761859/Argentina-5-Canada-0-match-report.html |access-date=22 May 2022 |website=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> At the World Cup, he helped Argentina reach the quarter-finals, playing in all five of Argentina's matches and starting four of them.<ref name=fifa/>

Following the World Cup, on 11 August 2010 Di María scored the first-ever international goal at [[Dublin]]'s new [[Aviva Stadium]] in a friendly against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] as Argentina won 1–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=Republic of Ireland 0–1 Argentina|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2010/0811/argentina.html |work=RTÉ Sport |date=11 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100814133729/https://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2010/0811/argentina.html |access-date=11 August 2010 |archive-date=14 August 2010 }}</ref>

Di María appeared three times during the [[2011 Copa América]], scoring once in a 3–0 defeat of [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] in the group stage.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.zonalmarking.net/2011/07/12/argentina-3-0-costa-rica-batista-finally-changes-system-and-argentina-progress/|title=Argentina 3–0 Costa Rica: Batista finally changes system, and Argentina progress|date=12 July 2011|work=Zonal Marking|access-date=1 July 2015|archive-date=7 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200307172951/http://www.zonalmarking.net/2011/07/12/argentina-3-0-costa-rica-batista-finally-changes-system-and-argentina-progress/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== 2011–2014: World Cup finals loss ===
Di María made 12 appearances during the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2014 FIFA World Cup qualification campaign]]<ref name=fifa/> and was included in the Argentina national team for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|tournament finals]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina World Cup 2014 squad |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/argentina/10810410/Argentina-World-Cup-2014-squad.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/argentina/10810410/Argentina-World-Cup-2014-squad.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Telegraph |date=2 June 2014 |access-date=2 July 2014 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> In Argentina's [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|round of 16]] match against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]], Di María scored the only goal of the game after 118 minutes, from a [[Lionel Messi]] assist.<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina 1–0 Switzerland |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27990606 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=1 July 2014 |access-date=2 June 2014 }}</ref> During the quarter-final match against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]], Di María suffered a muscle tear in the thigh and was later taken off the field. It was later announced after the match that Di María would miss the rest of the tournament due to the injury.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fifield |first=Dominic |date=2014-07-05 |title=Argentina's Ángel di María ruled out of World Cup with thigh injury |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jul/05/argentina-angel-di-maria-out-world-cup-thigh-injury |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Observer |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref> He had previously helped to create [[Gonzalo Higuaín]]'s only goal of the match, which sent Argentina into the semi-finals. Argentina finished the tournament as runners-up to [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Germany 1–0 Argentina |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28181689 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=13 July 2014 |access-date=27 August 2014 }}</ref>

On 11 July, Di María was named on the ten-man shortlist for FIFA's [[2014 FIFA World Cup#Golden Ball|Golden Ball]] award for the tournament's best player.<ref>{{cite news |title=World Cup 2014: Fifa announces Golden Ball shortlist |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28274011 |publisher=BBC Sport (British Broadcasting Corporation) |date=11 July 2014 |access-date=12 July 2014 }}</ref>

On 3 September 2014, in a friendly away against world champions Germany, Di María had a part in all four of Argentina's goals in a 4–2 victory, assisting three and scoring one.<ref>{{cite web |title=Highlights: Germany 2–4 Argentina – Angel Di Maria inspires win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29062991 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=25 August 2020 |date=4 September 2014 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== 2015–2020: Back-to-back Copa América finals losses and World Cup disappointment ===
[[File:Ángel Di María 2018.jpg|alt=Di Maria and the rest of the Argentina National Team starting eleven for the match against Nigeria.|thumb|Di María for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] during the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]
On 28 May 2015, Di María was included in Argentina national team for the [[2015 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/argentina/story/2470155/argentina-copa-america-squad-includes-angel-di-maria|title=Argentina's Copa America squad includes Man United's Angel Di Maria|date=28 May 2015|publisher=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Argentina 2015 Copa América Squad |url=https://africa.espn.com/football/team/squad/_/id/202/league/CONMEBOL.AMERICA/season/2015 |access-date=2025-04-13 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On 6 June, he was selected to [[Captain (association football)|captain]] the team in the absence of Lionel Messi for a warm-up match against [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]], scoring twice in a 5–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33039786|title=Sergio Aguero and Angel Di Maria score in Argentina win over Bolivia|date=7 June 2015|publisher=BBC}}</ref> A week later, in their opening match of the tournament against Paraguay in [[La Serena, Chile|La Serena]], Di María won a penalty which Messi scored in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite news|title=Argentina 2–2 Paraguay|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33081605|access-date=14 June 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=14 June 2015}}</ref> On 30 June, he scored twice and assisted a goal for [[Sergio Agüero]], as Argentina defeated Paraguay 6–1 to reach [[2015 Copa América Final|the final]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Emons|first1=Michael|title=Argentina 6–1 Paraguay|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33085956|access-date=1 July 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=1 July 2015}}</ref> He was substituted with a hamstring injury within the first half-hour of the final against hosts [[Chile national football team|Chile]], which his team lost in a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] after a goalless draw.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hill |first=Tim |date=2015-07-04 |title=Chile win Copa América after beating Argentina on penalties – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2015/jul/04/copa-america-2015-final-chile-argentina-live |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=the Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In Argentina's opening match of the [[Copa América Centenario]] on 6 June 2016, a rematch of the previous tournament's final against defending champions Chile, Di María scored the opening goal of the match and later assisted [[Éver Banega]]'s goal in a 2–1 win. Di María dedicated the goal to his grandmother, who had recently died.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fisher |first=Ben |date=2016-06-07 |title=Argentina top Chile in rematch of last year's Copa América final |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jun/07/argentina-top-chile-in-rematch-of-last-years-copa-america-final |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> In his nation's second group match, against [[Panama national football team|Panama]] on 10 June, he assisted [[Nicolás Otamendi]]'s opening goal, but was later forced off due to injury. Argentina won the match 5–0.<ref>{{Cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=2016-06-11 |title=Lionel Messi scores brilliant hat-trick as Argentina surge into quarter-finals |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jun/10/lionel-messi-hat-trick-argentina-panama-copa-america |access-date=2025-04-13 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He missed the rest of the tournament due to injury<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/12452/copa-america/2016/06/24/24985212/di-maria-in-serious-doubt-for-copa-america-final|title=Di Maria in serious doubt for Copa America final|work=Goal (website)|author1=David Manuca|date=24 June 2016|access-date=17 July 2016}}</ref> as Argentina reached the [[Copa América Centenario Final|Copa América final]] for the second consecutive time, once again losing out to Chile on penalties, following a 0–0 draw.<ref name="Messi retirement">{{cite news |date=27 June 2016 |title=Lionel Messi retires from Argentina after Copa America final loss to Chile|url=http://www.espnfc.com/copa-america/story/2902891/lionel-messi-flags-potential-argentina-retirement-after-penalty-loss-to-chile|work=ESPN FC}}</ref>

Di María made 18 appearances in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2018 FIFA World Cup qualification campaign]].
